hard_case: the inline array holds the variable `n`, so the rule-2 reader collects no assertion although the callback runs and fails

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

reasoning: `return amount - 10` becomes `return amount - 20`. The test declares `const n = 150` and runs `[150, n].forEach((v) => { expect(capPriceVar(v)).toBe(140); })`; the callback runs for both elements and `capPriceVar(150)` returns 130, so the test fails. RIPR-SPEC-0246 example 5: an array holding a non-literal element collects no assertion. ripr reads no oracle in the test (`unknown`) and reports `weakly_exposed`, as the spec states; against the discriminated truth that is a false actionable gap the spec accepts.
